title: Inflammatory Biomarkers, Comorbidity, and Neurocognition in Women With Newly Diagnosed Breast Cancer
journal: JNCI Journal of the National Cancer Institute
notes: Pre-treatment cross-sectional study. Cytokines measured before surgery. sTNF-RII (soluble TNF receptor type II, proxy for TNF activity) was only cytokine independently predicting memory. IL-1ra elevated in patients vs controls (P=.007) but not predictor of cognition. Comorbidity predicted executive function and processing speed (P=.03 each). Instruments: DKEF battery approximated to Stroop (exec inhibition), WAIS-IV PSI approximated to TMT-B (processing speed), HVLT direct match. sTNF-RII is not identical to TNF-alpha — it's the soluble receptor which reflects TNF system activation.
effect_size_notes: Regression B for log(sTNF-RII) → memory T-scores converted to partial r via t-stat, then to d via 2r/sqrt(1-r^2). Partial r = -0.162 after adjusting for 10 covariates. d = -0.329. This is a partial/adjusted effect — represents unique variance explained by sTNF-RII after removing shared variance with covariates.
